reply.title: Why does a sigmoid squash any number into 0 to 1?
reply.story:
When building models that make binary choices, we often need to turn any real number into a probability between zero and one. Linear functions fail here because they grow without bound. We need a smooth, S-shaped curve that maps the entire number line into a strictly bounded output range.

Pierre François Verhulst faced a similar challenge in population dynamics, leading to the logistic function. By dividing a constant growth rate by an expanding capacity term, he found a curve that accelerates, then gracefully decelerates as it approaches a limit.

The logistic sigmoid formula achieves this by placing an exponential term in the denominator. As the input grows toward positive infinity, the exponential vanishes and the output approaches one. As the input drops toward negative infinity, the exponential dominates and the output approaches zero.
